**Visual observations:**
- Affected part: leaf (upper surface shown)
- Small, discrete lesions scattered across the leaf
- Lesions are circular to irregular, dark brown/reddish-brown centers
- Some lesions appear to have a slightly lighter center with darker margins
- One prominent lesion (right side) shows a circular shape with a distinct darker ring/border
- No yellowing halos, no water-soaking, no vein-limited angular lesions
- No white powdery coating, no mold, no pustules visible
- Lesions are small and scattered — not coalescing into large blotches yet

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Frogeye_leaf_spot**: Circular lesions with gray centers and reddish-brown borders — the prominent circular lesion with the ring pattern matches this well. Lesions are irregular to circular, gray center with dark red-brown margins. This fits well.
- **Septoria_brown_spot**: Small, dark brown irregularly shaped lesions on both leaf surfaces — possible, but typically starts lower canopy and lesions are more uniformly dark without the gray center.
- **Bacterial_Blight**: Angular, water-soaked spots with yellow-green halos — no halos visible here, doesn't fit.
- **Phyllosticta_leaf_spot**: Tan/brownish with purplish margins, lower canopy — possible but less distinctive circular pattern.
- **Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus**: Lesions along veins — the lesions here are not vein-associated.

The key distinguishing feature is the circular lesion with a clear gray-to-light-brown center and distinct reddish-brown border, which is the hallmark of **Frogeye leaf spot**. The scattered small discrete circular spots also fit this diagnosis well.
